newsitem.title: USA: U.S. grain dealers taking protection on corn, soy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grain dealers taking protection on corn, soy.

text.p: In anticipation of a lower opening in CBOT futures, U.S. grain dealers were taking five to ten cents per bushel scattered protection on soybeans and one to two cents protection on corn.
"We're taking a little flat-price protection this morning," said one Iowa merchandiser.
Dealers said they were taking five to seven cents protection per bushel on old crop soybeans and ten cents on new crop November soybeans.
Protection of one to two cents per bushel was being taken on all corn contracts, dealers said.
CBOT corn futures were expected to open one to three cents per bushel lower and soybeans were seen three to ten cents lower.
Markets were seen under pressure from good growing weather in the U.S. Midwest.
